d.why: The U.S. Secretary of State speaks at the Geneva summit and in the CIA meeting, but his credited name is only a job title, so he stays out.
The old woman in Felipe Carrillo Puerto tells Nakia about her rescue by K'uk'ulkan, but her credited name is only a description, not a name.
Dr. Graham is the CIA mineralogist running the vibranium search at sea; she gives orders, fights the Talokanil and is killed by Namor in the attack that starts the film's conflict.

The MIT faculty member's only film scene is asking Tony Stark about grant money for a hot-dog idea in Civil War, a short scene that changes nothing (his Ironheart role is TV, where the name rule still stands).
The Hydra officer in Tonsberg only orders the sarcophagus opened in one short scene, and his credited name is a rank, not a name.
Gabe Jones is a freed POW who joins the Howling Commandos, translates German to drive the Hydra tank, and arrests Arnim Zola on the train, with lines throughout.
Jacques Dernier is the French Howling Commando and explosives man who breaks out of the Hydra camp, joins Steve's unit after talking in French with Gabe Jones, and blows up a Hydra tank.
Falsworth is the British officer freed from the Hydra camp who fires the stolen tank's cannon, joins the Howling Commandos and fights in the raid on Hydra headquarters, with lines.
Sergeant Duffy is Steve Rogers' drill sergeant who runs the Project Rebirth recruits through basic training, setting up the flagpole test Steve wins and barking orders in the fake-grenade scene.
Councilman Singh of the World Security Council presses Pierce over the Lemurian Star and Fury, then defies Pierce once Hydra is exposed and is killed by his explosive badge.
The Skrull who shoots at Vers and fights her on the train (dropping the memory crystal) has a real part, but he is credited only by a description ('Surfer Skrull' / 'Skrull Spy'), not a name.
In Captain Marvel she is only one of the Skrull refugees on Mar-Vell's lab with no lines or part, and her credited name is a description.
Norex is Talos's science officer who chases Vers to Earth, poses as Maria Rambeau, refits the Quadjet for space and stays behind as Carol's decoy until Yon-Rogg kills him.
The Kaecilius follower who kills Sol Rama is credited only by her hair colour, a description and not a name, like the Tall Zealot.
The Zealot whom Kaecilius stabs along with the Ancient One is credited only by a physical description; the owner ruled him out.
The Zealot whom Strange kicks into the desert is credited only by her hair colour, a description and not a name.
Strange's therapist tells him about Pangborn and sends him the file, but his credited name is only a job description.
The Zealot who doubts Kaecilius and is killed when his ritual fails is credited only by a trait, not a name.
Master Hamir shows Strange magic with one hand and guards America Chavez until the Scarlet Witch kills him, but he has no lines in either film.
The Hong Kong Sanctum's master only comes through a portal and greets Wong before the battle, a short scene that changes nothing, and her credited name is a title.
Stakar's bearded Ravager just follows Stakar around and salutes at Yondu's funeral, and his credited name is a description.
Brahl is a Yondu Ravager who guards Yondu on Contraxia, taunts Rocket on Berhert, sides with Taserface's mutiny and throws Yondu's loyalists out the airlock before Yondu kills him.
Mainframe is the Ravager captain on Stakar's old team who rejoins them in Vol. 2 and warns the Guardians they're being boarded by the United Ravagers in Vol. 3, speaking in both films.
Retch is a Ravager who plots the mutiny with Taserface, torments Groot on the Eclector, and is thrown to his death by Groot during Yondu's escape.
Tullk is the veteran Ravager who defends Yondu against Taserface's talk of mutiny and is thrown out the airlock in front of Yondu for staying loyal.
The Knowhere vendor is just a background resident at the party and the battle, with no part, and her credited name is a description.
Behemoth is the High Evolutionary's talking bird-like Hell Spawn guard who scans Nebula's arm, escorts Quill and Groot, and leads the attack on Knowhere until Cosmo crushes him.
Kwol is the Orgoscope administrator who spots Mantis and Drax and sends the Orgosentries after the Guardians before Gamora shoots her in the leg.
